selectedOriginals.caption: Details of Trevi Fountain, Rome, Italy
selectedOriginals.inspection: 2006 papal crest original individually inspected: large shield with three diagonal bands and horizontal band, curled border/scrollwork, triple-crown papal tiara/crossed keys above, seated winged trumpet figures flanking shield, festoon relief below. Original sculptural silhouette required; no copied inscription or photographic texture.

selectedOriginals.caption: Trevi Fountain, Rome
selectedOriginals.inspection: 2022 frontal original individually inspected: broad pale travertine facade, three window bays on each wing with triangular lower pediments and round upper pediments, four projecting giant Corinthian columns around central triumphal arch, small-column curved lower portico, coffered half dome, side statues/upper reliefs. Tall central attic bears four allegorical figures, balustrade and papal crest. Turquoise basin/rough rockwork distinct; people and neighbors excluded.

additionalInspected.inspection: 2010 HDR oblique plaza original individually inspected: curved thick basin coping, stepped pedestrian amphitheatre, stone bollards/iron rails, actual right-side narrow stairs between rock and wall. Water and rock occupy different outlines; broad dry approach remains outside basin. Facade scale/column/window depth visible; surrounding city/crowds/lamps excluded.

additionalInspected.caption: Fontaine de Trevi, l'Océan jaillit de sa niche, juché sur un char tiré par deux chevaux marins et deux tritons
additionalInspected.inspection: 2011 central sculpture original individually inspected: Oceanus torso turns above draped forward leg on shell chariot, two distinct rearing sea horses and tritons leaning at their flanks, side allegorical female figures in rectangular niches. Four small columns support curved entablature below coffered half dome. Multi-stage curved spill basins and waterfall drops below rockwork; recognizable conservative silhouettes rather than exact facial reproduction.

additionalInspected.caption: Fontaine de Trevi, Rome.
additionalInspected.inspection: 2021 left oblique original individually inspected: actual deep facade profile, giant column capitals/pilaster order and square rusticated lower plinth, multiple cornice/attic tiers, rectangular relief panels and distinct window pediments/balustrades. Short side return wall and palace beyond distinguish scope. No police car, bollards or people replicated from foreground.

additionalInspected.caption: Fontana di Trevi
additionalInspected.inspection: 2012 close rock/water original individually inspected: layered rounded spill bowls, actual waterfall curtains over irregular rocky lips, deep negative crevices, projecting irregular travertine ledges and warm calcified stains. Distinct calm/rearing horses and poses. Restrained pale rock mesh/blue-green water; no copied photo pixels or frozen photographic foam.

scope: Fountain basin, rockwork, central arch and immediately backing Palazzo Poli facade; sculpture as restrained recognizable silhouettes. Full palace north of immediate facade, neighbors, streets, people/cars and signs excluded.

primarySources.title: Rome cultural authority: Fontana di Trevi, mostra dell’acqua vergine
primarySources.inspection: Primary structural/material description read: triumphal arch facade with deep niche, broad rockwork and basin, Oceanus on shell chariot with two differently posed sea horses/tritons; travertine,marble,plaster,stucco,metal. Official source is descriptive, not a measured construction plan.

primarySources.title: Official Rome tourism: Palazzo Poli–Fontana di Trevi
primarySources.inspection: Official account confirms fountain is inserted into rear facade of Palazzo Poli; full palace comprises multiple enlargements. Supports bounded fountain/facade identity, not reproduction of the entire palace.

limitations: Native map geometry is quantized and low-zoom; precise sculpted rock placement and facade heights are photographic interpretations, not a construction survey.
Native whole-fountain envelope differs from actual water edge. Preserve both; do not fill the whole envelope with water.
Mapped Palazzo Poli has rear courts and wings; asset scope covers fountain facade and immediate backing thickness, not complete palace or its interior.
Statues, arms, horses, shell chariot and papal crest must retain interpreted recognizable silhouettes; no exact facial/inscription/art-conservation reproduction.
Native map preparation establishes location and signed axes; geometry, independent terrain and actual visual/placement acceptance must be separately verified before any completion annotation.
